title: Central Maine Ghost Hunters take on historically haunted Vassalboro mill
excerpt: On Saturday, you can get an inside look at a hunt yourself.
content:
VASSALBORO, Maine (WABI) - What’s Halloween without a haunting?

Searching for the unseen is the specialty of Central Maine Ghost Hunters, a team of about 10 that has ventured into places others would run from for over a decade.

“I’ve had experiences growing up and I watched the shows,” explained Dustin Marcia, founder and lead investigator. “I said, ‘I can probably do this.’ So I said, ‘Let’s try it,’ talked to a buddy of mine, let’s try it, see what we can do. And sure enough, it’s come here.”

Along with house calls, the crew visits supposedly haunted locations. WABI joined them on their investigation into the old American Woolen Company Mill in Vassalboro.

Local man Ray Breton bought the property for $35,500 in 2010.

“Late 1700s, the wooden building burned, and then, so they started with putting brick buildings up. So, the wings are all different. They’re dated almost for every war there was,” Breton described. “The building you walk through, the wing here is 1850. This wing here, once you walk through the brick causeway, this is 1917, First World War.”

He says as the mill was considered the largest on the Eastern Seaboard, employment peaked at about 500 people. With that, many accidents had been logged over the years, including 33 drownings over 100 years, electrocutions, and someone allegedly being pushed down the elevator shaft.

Over the years, Breton says one spirit has made himself especially noticeable. Called “The Captain,” an old man wearing what looks to be a captain’s hat can be seen in the back of photographs and first-hand accounts.

To speak with spirits, Central Maine Ghost Hunters use electromagnetic sensors, lights, radio waves and bells to reach the other side.

Despite the name, they say they’re more in the business of helping ghosts rather than hunting them.

“People need help and we try to help people. Even if they don’t have anything at their homes, at least give them a peace of mind,” Marcia said. “And we try to, if we can, try to help the spirits move on.“

On Saturday, you can get an inside look at a hunt yourself!

Saturday from 6 p.m. to 11 p.m., Central Maine Ghost Hunters are inviting the public to the Giberson Funeral Home in Bingham for a meet and greet before a 4-hour investigation of the building.

Tickets are $40 for general admission and $60 for VIP.
